clue.text: Small group infiltrating Irish loyalists

indicators.note: to infiltrate is to get inside a group, so the small group sits within the Irish name

blocks.note: Pat is a stock Irish name, standing for an Irishman
a trio is a group of three
S is the abbreviation for small, as on clothing labels

explanation.surface: A small cell has worked its way into an Irish loyalist organisation.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Small group' reads as one phrase, but Small gives its own letter, placed at the end.
explanation.definitionFit: Patriots are people devoted to their country, which is exactly what loyalists claim to be.

clue.text: Minor part of speech is in writing at bottom of page

indicators.note: in a down answer, being at the bottom of something means coming after it

blocks.note: p is the abbreviation for page
an article is a piece of writing

explanation.surface: A grammar note about a small word written at the foot of the page.
explanation.definitionFit: In grammar, a particle is a small uninflected word such as up in give up, a lesser part of speech.

clue.text: Schedule for US magazine board

blocks.note: Time is an American news magazine
a board is a table, as in board and lodging

explanation.surface: An American magazine's board of directors sets out its plan.
explanation.definitionFit: A timetable sets out when things happen, the same as a schedule of events or departures.

clue.text: Private's on target

blocks.note: first meaning: personal, not shown outwardly
second meaning: the ring next to the bull on an archery or shooting target

explanation.surface: An army private hits the mark.
explanation.walkthrough: Private looks like a soldier, but it is the adjective.
explanation.definitionFit: Inner feelings are private ones, and on a target the ring just outside the bull is called by this word.

clue.text: Minor gets four or six in test

indicators.note: the test gets something placed inside it, taking it in

blocks.note: a trial is a test
IV is four in Roman numerals

explanation.surface: A junior cricketer hits a boundary in a Test match.
explanation.walkthrough: Four or six sounds like cricket boundaries; the joke is that IV and VI, four and six, both work, since TRIVIAL holds either.
explanation.definitionFit: Something trivial is of little importance, the same as minor.

clue.text: It's available in pearls, priced higher than rubies

definitions.text: It's available in pearls, priced higher than rubies

blocks.clueFragment: It's available in pearls, priced higher than rubies
blocks.note: surface reading: something sold in a jeweller's, dearer than precious stones

blocks.clueFragment: It's available in pearls, priced higher than rubies
blocks.note: setter's reading: the quality of the phrase 'pearls of ...', which the Book of Proverbs says is above rubies

explanation.surface: A jeweller describes some luxury item stocked in pearl that costs more than rubies.
explanation.walkthrough: Two familiar phrases are joined: 'pearls of wisdom' and Proverbs, 'the price of wisdom is above rubies'.
explanation.definitionFit: Good sense is the thing people quote in wise sayings and that the Bible ranks as more precious than jewels.

clue.text: Artlessness of some of Blake's songs

blocks.note: first meaning: simplicity, lack of guile
second meaning: William Blake's poems in Songs of ...

explanation.surface: Blake's lyrics are notably naive and simple.
explanation.definitionFit: Being guileless and naive is lack of worldliness, and Blake wrote a poetry collection, Songs of Innocence.

clue.text: Played attacking shot for crowd

blocks.note: first meaning: past tense of drive, a forceful stroke in cricket or golf
second meaning: a large moving herd or throng

explanation.surface: A batsman plays an aggressive stroke to please the spectators.
explanation.definitionFit: A drive is a forceful hitting stroke, so the past tense fits; a drove is a herd of animals or a throng of people.

clue.text: Violent action has potential to give you the edge

blocks.note: may expresses possibility, as in it may happen
a hem is the edge of cloth

explanation.surface: Violence could give you an advantage over rivals.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Give you the edge' sounds like gaining an advantage, but edge simply means the border of a garment.
explanation.definitionFit: Mayhem is chaos and violent disorder; in old law it meant maiming a person.

clue.text: Initially, this has the sound of an open profession

blocks.clueFragment: Initially, this has the sound of an open
blocks.note: surface reading: something that begins by sounding frank and candid

blocks.clueFragment: Initially, this has the sound of an open
blocks.note: setter's reading: the answer begins with a vowel, an open sound, and when said aloud sounds like 'a vowel'

explanation.surface: A declaration that sounds frank, at least at first.
explanation.walkthrough: Vowels are open sounds, made without closing the mouth; the answer both starts with one and, spoken, sounds like the phrase 'a vowel'.
explanation.definitionFit: An avowal is a frank declaration, so it is a profession made openly, as in a profession of faith.

clue.text: Italian writing in French

blocks.note: first meaning: a native of Rome, a person from Italy
second meaning: the French word for a novel

explanation.surface: An Italian author who writes in French.
explanation.definitionFit: A Roman is someone from Italy's capital, and in French a novel, a long piece of writing, is called by the same word.

clue.text: Designer cutlery finally put in catalogue

indicators.note: finally points to the very end of the word it follows, so only its closing letter is kept

blocks.note: an inventor is someone who designs new things
the final letter of cutlery

explanation.surface: A designer's line of cutlery is finally included in the sales catalogue.
explanation.definitionFit: An inventory is a complete itemised list of goods, the same thing as a catalogue of stock.

clue.text: Struggle in winter broadcast to get audience

indicators.note: seed that is broadcast is scattered widely, so the letters of winter are thrown into a new order
in places the struggle inside the rearranged letters of the season

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged
to vie is to struggle or compete

explanation.surface: A broadcaster battles through winter to reach the people listening in.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Broadcast' and 'audience' suggest radio listeners, but audience here means a formal meeting.
explanation.definitionFit: An audience is a formal meeting with an important person, such as the Pope, and an interview is a similar formal meeting.

clue.text: Possibly one silk fabric or another used in church

indicators.note: used in puts the other cloth inside the abbreviation for the church

blocks.note: CE is the Church of England
another fabric: rep is a corded cloth used for upholstery

explanation.surface: Choosing between silk fabrics for vestments or hangings in a church.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Another' means another fabric, so it supplies a cloth name of its own.
explanation.definitionFit: Crêpe de Chine is a fine silk, so this crinkled cloth may be one made of silk.

clue.text: Free to be defamatory about artist

indicators.note: about means surrounding, so the defaming word wraps round the painter

blocks.note: libel is defamatory writing
RA is a Royal Academician, an artist

explanation.surface: Someone claims the right to say damaging things about a painter.
explanation.definitionFit: Liberal can mean unrestricted or generous, as in a liberal helping, the same as free.

clue.text: Form new congregation with spiritual instruction and prayer

blocks.note: RE is religious education, taught in British schools
a collect is a short prayer in the church service

explanation.surface: A minister founds a new congregation through teaching and prayer.
explanation.walkthrough: Read as re-collect, gathering together again, it means forming a new assembly.
explanation.definitionFit: To re-collect is to gather people together again, and gathering a new group is forming a congregation.

clue.text: Continue to yearn for a position in the field

blocks.note: to long is to yearn
on, as in carry on, means continue

explanation.surface: Someone keeps on hankering after a particular job or place in the field.
explanation.walkthrough: Long on is a cricket fielding position, deep on the leg side behind the bowler.
explanation.definitionFit: In cricket, the fielders are placed in named spots, and long on is one of those named places.

clue.text: Be more than exhausted, more stupefied

blocks.note: out means used up, as when supplies are out
the comparative of numb, stupefied

explanation.surface: Someone is beyond tired, utterly dazed.
explanation.walkthrough: The second part is read as numb-er, more numb, not the word for a figure.
explanation.definitionFit: To outnumber a group is to exceed it in count, being more numerous.

clue.text: Rally jolly supportive of engineers' leader

indicators.note: in a down answer a supporting part sits underneath, so it comes after what it holds up

blocks.note: RE is the Royal Engineers
CO is a commanding officer
jolly, as in jolly good, means very

explanation.surface: A rally of supporters cheers the engineers' leader.
explanation.walkthrough: Rally looks like a mass meeting, but it means a revival after a setback.
explanation.definitionFit: A rally is a revival in strength or prices after a fall, which is what a recovery is.

clue.text: D'Artagnan, for example, as one who receives the queen

blocks.note: a fence receives stolen goods
R is for Regina, Latin for queen

explanation.surface: D'Artagnan, the Musketeer, received by the Queen of France.
explanation.walkthrough: The Musketeers' plot hinges on the queen, which makes 'receives the queen' sound like part of the story.
explanation.definitionFit: D'Artagnan, hero of The Three Musketeers, is a swordsman, and a sword fighter is an example of one who fights with blades.

clue.text: Forcibly remove cheat

blocks.note: first meaning: to tear something away
second meaning: to swindle someone

explanation.definitionFit: To tear a thing away is to pull it off violently, and in slang to overcharge or swindle someone is the same verb.

clue.text: Special rate available in the battle zone

indicators.note: something special has been made out of the ordinary, so these letters come in an unusual arrangement
available in places the reworked word inside the little word that follows

blocks.note: taken as written
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: A special price is on offer for those in the war zone.
explanation.walkthrough: 'The battle zone' looks like a whole phrase, but 'the' belongs to the wordplay.
explanation.definitionFit: A theatre of war is the region where fighting takes place, so the word alone can mean a combat area.

clue.text: Call for action from viewers

blocks.note: surface reading: television audiences demanding more excitement
setter's reading: the cry of huntsmen who have sighted the fox, urging the chase on

explanation.surface: Television audiences demand more excitement on screen.
explanation.walkthrough: The viewers are not watching television; they are huntsmen who have just seen the fox.
explanation.definitionFit: In foxhunting, the rider who spots the quarry shouts this cry to start the hounds and field after it.

clue.text: One removes locks and bolt to take place over, finally

indicators.note: finally points to the closing letter of the word just before it

blocks.note: a bar is a bolt on a door
to be is to exist or take place
the final letter of over

explanation.surface: A burglar takes out locks and bolts to break into a place.
explanation.walkthrough: Locks and bolt suggest a door, but the locks are hair.
explanation.definitionFit: A barber cuts men's hair, and locks of hair are what he takes off.

clue.text: Old coin as source of financial support

blocks.note: first meaning: an English gold coin of the 15th to 17th centuries
second meaning: a backer, especially of a stage show

explanation.surface: An antique coin offered up to fund something.
explanation.definitionFit: The old gold piece showed the archangel Michael, and a theatrical backer who puts up money is also called by that heavenly name.

clue.text: Outfit's increase in strength

blocks.note: first meaning: a set of clothes, often eye-catching
second meaning: as a wind rising, it gets up

explanation.surface: A firm grows more powerful.
explanation.walkthrough: Outfit looks like a company, but it is clothing.
explanation.definitionFit: A get-up is a costume or set of clothes, and the phrasal verb is used of wind or sea growing stronger.

clue.text: Communist planners built poor construction

indicators.note: a construction is something put together, so these letters are assembled anew

blocks.note: taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Soviet planners put up shoddy buildings.
explanation.definitionFit: The policy committee of a Communist party, which directed the state's plans, is named this.

clue.text: Achieved harmony in what one did

indicators.note: in says the letters sit inside the following words, across their joins

blocks.note: the letters run from the end of what through one into did

explanation.surface: Someone managed to agree in all they did.
explanation.definitionFit: Colours or sounds that tone together go well with each other, which is achieving harmony.

clue.text: Alternative to crawling for insect

blocks.note: first meaning: a swimming stroke, an alternative to front crawl
second meaning: the winged insect

explanation.surface: A caterpillar's crawling gives way to flight.
explanation.walkthrough: Crawling suggests a caterpillar, but it is the swimming stroke.
explanation.definitionFit: It names both a swimming stroke used instead of front crawl and a colourful winged insect.

clue.text: 23 August count is one

blocks.note: first meaning: like 23, an old English gold coin
second meaning: grand, dignified
third meaning: a member of the aristocracy, as a count is

explanation.walkthrough: August looks like the month, but it is the adjective meaning stately. 23 is the old coin clued at 23-across.
explanation.definitionFit: It is an old gold coin, an adjective for stately and dignified, and a member of the aristocracy, such as a count.

clue.text: Fame for traveller, brave type

blocks.note: a rep is a travelling sales representative
a brave is a Native American warrior, and the Ute are a Native American people

explanation.surface: A daring traveller wins renown.
explanation.walkthrough: In crosswords a brave is a Native American warrior, so a tribe name follows.
explanation.definitionFit: Repute is a person's reputation or standing, and high repute amounts to renown or celebrity.

clue.text: Take care of and dry our artificial fabric

indicators.note: something artificial is made up rather than natural, so these letters are made into a new order

blocks.note: c/o is the postal abbreviation for care of
taken as written, to be rearranged

explanation.surface: Laundry instructions: look after this synthetic material and dry it carefully.
explanation.walkthrough: 'Artificial fabric' reads as one phrase, but corduroy is usually cotton; artificial only signals the rearrangement.
explanation.definitionFit: Corduroy is a ribbed cotton cloth, so it is a kind of woven fabric.
